page: Microsoft Azure E48_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine built on Microsoft Hyper-V. The instance provides 48 vCPUs derived from 24 physical cores of an Intel Xeon Platinum 8370C processor running at a base clock speed of 2.8 GHz, supported by simultaneous multithreading. Memory resources total 384 GB of RAM, maintaining an 8 GB per vCPU ratio suitable for memory-bound architectures. The CPU architecture supports instruction sets including AVX-512, AVX512_VNNI, AES, VAES, and SHA_NI, backed by 48 MB of shared L3 cache and 1 MB of L2 cache per core. The instance includes no integrated local storage and no hardware GPU accelerators, requiring remote block storage for persistent data.

Benchmark evaluations highlight strong uncached memory bandwidth, reaching 252.4 GB/sec for large block reads and 126.65 GB/sec for writes. The platform delivers solid results in memory-centric and cryptographic workloads, evidenced by high PassMark memory ratings, strong database operation throughput, and elevated CPU encryption scores. Computational benchmarks across Geekbench and stress-ng place general integer and multi-core processing within mid-tier expectations. While capable of moderate LLM prompt processing via AVX-512 extensions, generation throughput on large parameter models is constrained by the absence of discrete GPU hardware.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the E48_v5 provides a dense allocation of RAM per vCPU without the premium overhead associated with specialized accelerator hardware or integrated high-speed local NVMe drives. This configuration delivers an efficient profile for memory-heavy enterprise deployments that rely on centralized external storage fabrics. Primary workloads include large in-memory caching systems, enterprise relational databases, medium-scale data analytics, in-memory processing engines, and high-concurrency web serving tiers.
description: Microsoft Azure E48_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine equipped with 48 vCPUs and 384 GB of RAM, based on the Intel Xeon Platinum 8370C processor running at 2.8 GHz. Featuring 24 physical cores with multithreading and an x86_64 architecture, the platform includes advanced vector instruction sets including AVX-512 and VAES. The configuration contains no discrete GPU accelerators and omits local storage, relying on external network-attached volumes for data retention. Benchmark tests demonstrate strong large-block uncached memory read and write bandwidth alongside above-average PassMark database and cryptographic test results, while general compute metrics perform in the median range. This instance configuration is engineered for memory-intensive workloads that require substantial working memory, including enterprise relational databases, distributed in-memory caches, high-concurrency static web serving, and memory-bound transactional data systems.
